newsitem.title: INDIA: Nickel sinks, other metals quiet on Indian market.
newsitem.headline: Nickel sinks, other metals quiet on Indian market.

text.p: Nickel prices declined further on the Indian market on Friday, while other base metals remained quiet, dealers said.
Nickel moved down by 200 rupees at 36,800 rupees per quintal, reflecting world trends. Physical demand was dull and there was light profit-taking by the local stockist.
Nickel's latest declines come on top of a 200 rupee fall on Wednesday, and after a respite on Thursday.

Copper was quiet at 13,600 rupees per quintal so was zinc at 8,000 rupees and lead at 4,150 rupees per quintal amid limited activity. Trading volume was dull as major players awaited announcement by state-owned producers of June selling prices.
Copper's undercurrent was firm, reflecting expectations that state-owned producers will hike June prices after a recent upsurge in the world prices.
Tin was indicated at the previous level of 31,400 rupees, as was aluminium at 7,650 rupees per quintal amid nominal trading.
